newsitem.title: USA: Mass.judges congressional race decision expected.
newsitem.headline: Mass.judges congressional race decision expected.

text.p: Five Massachusetts justices are expected to decide who will be the Democratic nominee in the state's 10th congressional district within the next 48 hours.

Lawyers for both Democratic candidates, Philip Johnston and William Delahunt, estimated it would take the judges about five hours to go through the 956 punchcard ballots to determine if the dimples, dents, and squiggles are actually votes.

Holes in the punchcard ballots must be clean through for the electronic voting machines to count them, voting officials have said. The disputed ballots' holes, or chads as they are formally called, were only paritally punched or not punched through at all.

Johnston learned Friday while campaigning with first lady Hillary Clinton that a state court ruled Delahunt the winner of the Sept 17 Democratic primary. He filed an appeal to the state's highest court Monday asking a five-judge panel to review the ballots themselves.

Johnston 52, a liberal and former state representative who lacked funds for a television campaign in the primary, was initially declared the winner by a 206 vote margin. After a recount in selected districts certified by Secretary of State William Galvin, his lead had shrunk to 175.

But Norfolk Superior Court Judge Elizabeth Donovan ruled, after a review of more than 900 challenged ballots, that Delahunt, the Norfolk district attorney, actually won the race by 108 votes. She ordered Galvin to print new ballots with Delahunt's name.
Johnston's lawyer Dennis Newman told the justices of the Supreme Judicial court, "These inadvertent, inconsequential marks should not be not be counted as votes."
But Delahunt's lawyer, Michael Mone, argued that almost 1,000 people "would not have gone through a monsoon" not to cast their vote in the hotly contested race.

Meanwhile, the Republican nominee Edward Teague has been actively campaigning in the district which encompasses Cape Cod and the south shore of Massachusetts. He had started running television spots attacking Johnston, but pulled them after the judge's ruling.
The seat is being vacated by 12-term Democratic incumbent Gerry Studds, who is retiring.
